messages:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT — High error rate detected for /api/v1/generate in eu-central-1 (az a). ALB target group tg-0123 reporting 502/504 spikes. PagerDuty: PD-3892. Paging @oncall-eu. https://monitoring.redwood.example/alerts/PD-3892 :rotating_light:
Sarah Kim: ack — I'm oncall, looking. seeing sudden jump in 5xx from 03:12Z. users in eu reporting timeouts. sending first triage now.
Michael O'Connor: logs from envoy on pods in eu-central-1a show upstream reset errors: 
```
[2026-04-12T03:12:35Z] envoy upstream_reset: connection failure, remote closed
[2026-04-12T03:12:35Z] envoy error 502 from upstream target ip=10.0.45.23:8080
```
Sarah Kim: running quick curl against ALB (from eu-bastion): 
```
curl -v https://alb-euc-prod-123.eu-central-1.elb.amazonaws.com/api/v1/generate
* Connected to alb-euc-prod-123.eu-central-1.elb.amazonaws.com (18.194.xxx.xxx) port 443
* HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```
Priya Singh: can we confirm if it's app pod crash or underlying network/AZ fabric? I see node-level 'Connection reset by peer' across several pods in AZ a.
Alex Rivera: I can look at infra side (ALB/target groups). Quick check: ALB shows healthy hosts in az-b/c but many unhealthy in az-a. Might be node-level network flap. Recommend shutting down ALB targets in AZ a to stop routing traffic into flapping hosts while we investigate.
Michael O'Connor: agreed. We can deregister targets for tg-0123 in az-a. Command (aws cli):
```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-central-1:111122223333:targetgroup/tg-0123/abcdef --targets Id=i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h
```
Sarah Kim: before we do that — we should lower Route53 TTL to 30s to let DNS-level changes propagate if we want to fail over regionally. Changing TTL now.
deploy-bot: Route53 change requested: change-batch id r53-change-98765 created. New TTL 30s for service.example.com weighted records.
Priya Singh: I'm going to cordon nodes in eu-central-1a to prevent new pods landing there while we diagnose. `kubectl cordon <node>` and then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets` for the problematic nodes.
Sarah Kim: performing deregister now for target group tg-0123 in az-a (doing one by one). Monitoring error rate and latency.
(deployments/logs update)
Sarah Kim: 03:25Z — after removing az-a targets, error rate dropped ~85%. Latency back to 95th ~220ms. Still watching for residual 5xx from cached connections.
Alex Rivera: opening ticket with cloud provider for AZ network flap: case 2026-EC-1472. They acknowledge an incremental packet loss event in eu-central-1a ~03:05Z-03:30Z.
Michael O'Connor: next steps: keep az-a targets out of rotation until cloud confirms stable. Scale up pods in az-b/c by +30% to absorb traffic. K8s HPA should pick up but forcing a temporary scale to be safe. `kubectl scale deploy api --replicas=24 -n prod`
Priya Singh: scaling applied. New pods scheduled in az-b/c. Health checks on ALB now show healthy targets 60 in b/c, 0 in a.
Sarah Kim: Customer impact assessment: estimated ~12% of EU traffic failed between 03:05-03:26Z, mostly short-lived timeouts. No data loss, no auth anomalies. Notifying SRE lead + Customer Success for top-tier customers.
Alex Rivera: I'll take handoff when Sarah needs to step off in 20m. Current status: mitigated (traffic rerouted, targets drained). Cloud case open. Monitoring for 1hr post-fix.
Sarah Kim: handing off to Alex Rivera (next on-call) — timeline + actions in incident doc: https://confluence.redwood.example/incidents/PD-3892. Key notes: deregistered az-a targets, lowered DNS TTL, scaled az-b/c, cloud provider case 2026-EC-1472.
Alex Rivera: ack, taking over. I'll keep the channel posted and coordinate with CS for customer notifications. Reopen if errors reappear.
deploy-bot: Incident PD-3892 status -> mitigated. Duration 00:46: 03:05Z — 03:51Z.
Sarah Kim: thanks team :thumbsup: good recovery. I'll create a short postmortem draft and assign owners for next steps: (1) automate AZ drain on target-health fluctuation, (2) run DR test for AZ failure, (3) validate healthcheck sensitivity.
Alex Rivera: noted, will ensure follow-ups.
